content.text:
Yazi captures mouse input, so dragging goes to Yazi instead of Zellij’s text selection. Your Zellij already has `copy_on_select true`, but your [Yazi configuration](/home/thom/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles/home/home.nix:261) leaves mouse capture enabled.

Two options:

- **Quick workaround:** hold **Shift while dragging**, then use your terminal’s copy shortcut. This bypasses application mouse handling. [Zellij docs](https://zellij.dev/documentation/compatibility.html)
- **Make ordinary dragging copy text:** add this inside `programs.yazi`, rebuild your Home Manager configuration, and restart Yazi:
  ```nix
  settings.mgr.mouse_events = [];
  ```
  This disables Yazi’s mouse controls, allowing Zellij to handle selection and copy on release. You’ll use the keyboard to navigate Yazi. [Yazi docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/#mouse_events)

content.text: Yazi’s preview handles clicks and scrolling but has no built-in text-selection handler, so my earlier change doesn’t solve this. I’m removing it. I also found two viewers with application-level selection: `mdpad` documents copy on mouse release; `ink` documents drag selection followed by `y` and includes a file browser and Mermaid rendering.

You’re right—I missed that Zellij sees Yazi’s columns as one pane. I’ve reverted my change.

**Your Yazi version has no built-in preview text selection.** Its [preview implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sxyazi/yazi/v26.9.1/yazi-plugin/preset/components/preview.lua) handles clicks and scrolling, but not drag selection. Supporting this would require custom development.

For your Markdown-reading workflow, two alternatives stand out:

| Viewer | Selection | Other relevant features |
|---|---|---|
| [mdpad](https://www.lpalbou.info/mdpad/clipboard.html) | Drag rendered text; **copies automatically on release** | Search, keyboard navigation, editing |
| [ink](https://borghei.github.io/ink/) | Drag to select, then **`y` to copy** | File browser, tabs, inline Mermaid diagrams |

**mdpad matches your requested mouse behavior most closely.** Ink looks closer to your existing browsing and diagram workflow. These are documented capabilities; I haven’t yet tested either inside your Zellij setup.

content.text:
Right—I narrowed it too far. You need a general file browser with code/text previews and selection confined to the content.

**Neovim with a file-tree sidebar is a stronger candidate:** it handles text selection internally, supports code highlighting, and [nvim-tree](https://github.com/nvim-tree/nvim-tree.lua) provides keyboard-driven browsing. [Mouse dragging selects document text](https://neovim.io/doc/user/options/#'mouse'), excluding the sidebar and line numbers. Copy-on-release would need configuration.

Markdown presentation can be added with [render-markdown.nvim](https://github.com/MeanderingProgrammer/render-markdown.nvim), though that doesn’t establish parity with your current Mermaid previews.

I’d test that combination against your selection workflow before replacing Yazi. The Markdown-only viewers weren’t adequate recommendations for your needs.

content.text:
**Yes—Helix is worth trying first, especially since you already have it installed.** I should have considered it before suggesting Neovim.

Your installed **25.07.1** handles mouse dragging as document selection, so copying excludes line numbers and neighboring splits. It also copies on release to the **primary selection**—which is distinct from the regular clipboard. [Helix implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helix-editor/helix/25.07.1/helix-term/src/ui/editor.rs)

Try it now:

1. Run `hx .`, then **Space → f** to pick a file.
2. Drag over code or text without Shift.
3. Press **Space → y** to copy explicitly to the system clipboard. [Keybindings](https://docs.helix-editor.com/keymap.html)

The tradeoffs: your version uses a file picker rather than a persistent Yazi-style browser, and Markdown is syntax-highlighted source rather than a rendered preview.

Your clipboard provider is already `termcode` (OSC 52). **Automatic copy-on-release reaching your usual clipboard still needs checking through Zellij**, but Helix does have the application-level selection you need.

content.text:
**Partly, but Helix can’t provide that whole experience through configuration alone.**

| Requirement | Helix |
|---|---|
| Browse directories | **Already available:** `Space → e` opens the directory explorer. I missed this earlier—it shipped in your installed version. |
| Persistent Yazi-style columns/sidebar | The explorer is a temporary picker, not a persistent sidebar alongside the document. |
| Code highlighting and document-only mouse selection | Supported in opened files. |
| Rendered Markdown inside the document pane | No supported configuration for this. |
| External rendered Markdown preview | Possible with a companion tool such as `mpls`, including Mermaid diagrams. |

The [25.07 release notes](https://helix-editor.com/news/release-25-07-highlights/#file-explorer) describe the directory explorer. [`mpls`](https://github.com/mhersson/mpls) renders Markdown in a web browser; it doesn’t turn a Helix split into a rendered preview.

So Helix fits **browse → open → select/copy code or text**. If you need **persistent file browsing + rendered Markdown + code viewing + mouse selection in one terminal app**, stock Helix falls short. I wouldn’t replace your Yazi setup with it expecting all four.

content.text:
**I’d add selection to Yazi.** Your existing setup already gives you the browsing layout, code previews, rendered Markdown, and Mermaid diagrams you want. Selection is the missing capability. My earlier recommendations gave up too much of that.

| Route | Work required | My assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Extend Yazi** | Add selection, highlighting, and clipboard copying to text previews | Best fit; preserves your existing workflow |
| **Extend Helix** | Add a persistent browser **and** rendered Markdown with selection | Much broader changes to the editor |
| **Build a dedicated viewer** | Own browsing, rendering, navigation, selection, clipboard, and terminal compatibility | Most freedom, but substantially more maintenance |

For Yazi, **I’d investigate a plugin first, but accept a focused core patch if that produces a cleaner implementation.**

There are useful pieces already: Yazi dispatches mouse drag events to UI components and exposes a [clipboard API](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/plugins/utils/#clipboardtext). Your [Markdown previewer](https://github.com/WhoSowSee/mdv-previewer.yazi/blob/main/main.lua) also retains the rendered text as lines. Those make selection plausible without rebuilding the browser.

The uncertainty is **sharing the right text representation across previewers**. Yazi’s built-in code-preview API renders the file but doesn’t return its text to Lua. A Markdown-specific plugin might therefore be straightforward while a solution that also handles code cleanly needs core support. [Preview API](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/plugins/utils/#preview_codeopts)

I’d build a small proof of concept with these acceptance criteria:

- Drag within the preview; selection stays inside that preview.
- Release to copy to your normal clipboard through Zellij.
- Works for **both code and rendered Markdown**, including your Mermaid text diagrams.
- Preserves code indentation, excludes UI padding, and handles tabs and wide Unicode characters correctly.
- File changes, scrolling, and resizing cannot leave a selection pointing at stale content.

The important design choice is to base selection on the **preview’s text and layout**, rather than scrape the whole terminal. That also lets us distinguish real newlines from visual wrapping. A first implementation could select only visible text; extending selection while scrolling would follow.

If plugin support forces us to replace Yazi’s existing rendering or maintain two inconsistent selection implementations, I’d prefer a **small, pinned Yazi patch**, packaged through Nix and suitable for proposing upstream. I wouldn’t promise the patch is small until that proof of concept establishes where the text and layout are accessible.

**Keep Helix as the editor; make Yazi a better browser and reader.** A standalone custom app becomes worthwhile if your requirements grow into a substantially different reading interface—not yet for this missing interaction.
